feature:feature:martial-arts.description: At 1st level, your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and monk weapons, which are shortswords and any simple melee weapons that don't have the two- handed or heavy property. You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a shield: - You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and monk weapons. - You can roll a d4 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or monk weapon. This die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of Table: The Monk. - When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a monk weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and attack with a quarterstaff, you can also make an unarmed strike as a bonus action, assuming you haven't already taken a bonus action this turn. Certain monasteries use specialized forms of the monk weapons. For example, you might use a club that is two lengths of wood connected by a short chain (called a nunchaku) or a sickle with a shorter, straighter blade (called a kama). Whatever name you use for a monk weapon, you can use the game statistics provided for the weapon.

feature:feature:ki.description: Starting at 2nd level, your training allows you to harness the mystic energy of ki. Your access to this energy is represented by a number of ki points. Your monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Ki Points column of Table: The Monk. You can spend these points to fuel various ki features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind. You learn more ki features as you gain levels in this class. When you spend a ki point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or long rest, at the end of which you draw all of your expended ki back into yourself. You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your ki points. Some of your ki features require your target to make a saving throw to resist the feature's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows: Ki save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

feature:feature:flurry-of-blows.description: Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 1 ki point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.

feature:feature:patient-defense.description: You can spend 1 ki point to take the Dodge action as a bonus action on your turn.

feature:feature:step-of-the-wind.description: You can spend 1 ki point to take the Disengage or Dash action as a bonus action on your turn, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

feature:feature:unarmored-movement.description: Starting at 2nd level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain monk levels, as shown in Table: The Monk. At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.

feature:feature:monastic-tradition.description: When you reach 3rd level, you commit yourself to a monastic tradition, such as the Way of the Open Hand. Your tradition grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

feature:feature:deflect-missiles.description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use your reaction to deflect or catch the missile when you are hit by a ranged weapon attack. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can catch the missile if it is small enough for you to hold in one hand and you have at least one hand free. If you catch a missile in this way, you can spend 1 ki point to make a ranged attack with the weapon or piece of ammunition you just caught, as part of the same reaction. You make this attack with proficiency, regardless of your weapon proficiencies, and the missile counts as a monk weapon for the attack, which has a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet.

feature:feature:slow-fall.description: Beginning at 4th level, you can use your reaction when you fall to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your monk level.

feature:feature:stunning-strike.description: Starting at 5th level, you can interfere with the flow of ki in an opponent's body. When you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn.

feature:feature:ki-empowered-strikes.description: Starting at 6th level, your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

feature:feature:evasion.description: At 7th level, your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a blue dragon's lightning breath or a fireball spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

feature:feature:stillness-of-mind.description: Starting at 7th level, you can use your action to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed or frightened.

feature:feature:purity-of-body.description: At 10th level, your mastery of the ki flowing through you makes you immune to disease and poison.

feature:feature:tongue-of-the-sun-and-mo.description: Starting at 13th level, you learn to touch the ki of other minds so that you understand all spoken languages. Moreover, any creature that can understand a language can understand what you say.

feature:feature:diamond-soul.description: Beginning at 14th level, your mastery of ki grants you proficiency in all saving throws. Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can spend 1 ki point to reroll it and take the second result.

feature:feature:monk:timeless-body.description: At 15th level, your ki sustains you so that you suffer none of the frailty of old age, and you can't be aged magically. You can still die of old age, however. In addition, you no longer need food or water.

feature:feature:empty-body.description: Beginning at 18th level, you can use your action to spend 4 ki points to become invisible for 1 minute. During that time, you also have resistance to all damage but force damage. Additionally, you can spend 8 ki points to cast the astral projection spell, without needing material components. When you do so, you can't take any other creatures with you.

feature:feature:perfect-self.description: At 20th level, when you roll for initiative and have no ki points remaining, you regain 4 ki points.

feature:feature:divine-sense.description: The presence of strong evil registers on your senses like a noxious odor, and powerful good rings like heavenly music in your ears. As an action, you can open your awareness to detect such forces. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any celestial, fiend, or undead within 60 feet of you that is not behind total cover. You know the type (celestial, fiend, or undead) of any being whose presence you sense, but not its identity. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the hallow spell. You can use this feature a number of times equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier. When you finish a long rest, you regain all expended uses.

feature:feature:lay-on-hands.description: Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you take a long rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of hit points equal to your paladin level x 5. As an action, you can touch a creature and draw power from the pool to restore a number of hit points to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in your pool. Alternatively, you can expend 5 hit points from your pool of healing to cure the target of one disease or neutralize one poison affecting it. You can cure multiple diseases and neutralize multiple poisons with a single use of Lay on Hands, expending hit points separately for each one. This feature has no effect on undead and constructs.

feature:feature:spellcasting-paladin.description: By 2nd level, you have learned to draw on divine magic through meditation and prayer to cast spells as a cleric does.

feature:feature:divine-smite.description: Starting at 2nd level, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 5d8. The damage increases by 1d8 if the target is an undead or a fiend.

feature:feature:divine-health.description: By 3rd level, the divine magic flowing through you makes you immune to disease.

feature:feature:sacred-oath.description: When you reach 3rd level, you swear the oath that binds you as a paladin forever. Up to this time you have been in a preparatory stage, committed to the path but not yet sworn to it. Now you choose an oath, such as the Oath of Devotion. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 15th, and 20th level. Those features include oath spells and the Channel Divinity feature.

feature:feature:oath-spells.description: Each oath has a list of associated spells. You gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description. Once you gain access to an oath spell, you always have it prepared. Oath spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain an oath spell that doesn't appear on the paladin spell list, the spell is nonetheless a paladin spell for you.

feature:feature:channel-divinity.description: Your oath allows you to channel divine energy to fuel magical effects. Each Channel Divinity option provided by your oath explains how to use it. When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which option to use. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Channel Divinity again. Some Channel Divinity effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your paladin spell save DC.

feature:feature:aura-of-protection.description: Starting at 6th level, whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you must make a saving throw, the creature gains a bonus to the saving throw equal to your Charisma modifier (with a minimum bonus of +1). You must be conscious to grant this bonus. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

feature:feature:aura-of-courage.description: Starting at 10th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be frightened while you are conscious. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

feature:feature:improved-divine-smite.description: By 11th level, you are so suffused with righteous might that all your melee weapon strikes carry divine power with them. Whenever you hit a creature with a melee weapon, the creature takes an extra 1d8 radiant damage. If you also use your Divine Smite with an attack, you add this damage to the extra damage of your Divine Smite.

feature:feature:cleansing-touch.description: Beginning at 14th level, you can use your action to end one spell on yourself or on one willing creature that you touch. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.

feature:feature:aura-improvements.description: At 18th level, the range of your auras increase to 30 feet.

feature:feature:favored-enemy-1-type.description: Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy. Choose a type of favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs) as favored enemies. You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them. When you gain this feature, you also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favored enemies, if they speak one at all. You choose one additional favored enemy, as well as an associated language, at 6th and 14th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of monsters you have encountered on your adventures.

feature:feature:natural-explorer-1-terra.description: You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in. While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits: - Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel. - Your group can't become lost except by magical means. - Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger. - If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace. - When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would. - While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area. You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.

feature:feature:spellcasting-ranger.description: By the time you reach 2nd level, you have learned to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells, much as a druid does.

feature:feature:ranger-archetype.description: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate, such as the Hunter. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

feature:feature:primeval-awareness.description: Beginning at 3rd level, you can use your action and expend one ranger spell slot to focus your awareness on the region around you. For 1 minute per level of the spell slot you expend, you can sense whether the following types of creatures are present within 1 mile of you (or within up to 6 miles if you are in your favored terrain): aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead. This feature doesn't reveal the creatures' location or number.

feature:feature:favored-enemy-2-types.description: Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy. Choose a type of favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs) as favored enemies. You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them. When you gain this feature, you also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favored enemies, if they speak one at all. You choose one additional favored enemy, as well as an associated language, at 6th and 14th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of monsters you have encountered on your adventures.

feature:feature:natural-explorer-2-terra.description: You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in. While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits: - Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel. - Your group can't become lost except by magical means. - Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger. - If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace. - When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would. - While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area. You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.

feature:feature:land-s-stride.description: Starting at 8th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard. In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such those created by the entangle spell.

feature:feature:natural-explorer-3-terra.description: You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in. While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits: - Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel. - Your group can't become lost except by magical means. - Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger. - If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace. - When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would. - While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area. You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.

feature:feature:hide-in-plain-sight.description: Starting at 10th level, you can spend 1 minute creating camouflage for yourself. You must have access to fresh mud, dirt, plants, soot, and other naturally occurring materials with which to create your camouflage. Once you are camouflaged in this way, you can try to hide by pressing yourself up against a solid surface, such as a tree or wall, that is at least as tall and wide as you are. You gain a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks as long as you remain there without moving or taking actions. Once you move or take an action or a reaction, you must camouflage yourself again to gain this benefit.

feature:feature:favored-enemy-3-enemies.description: Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy. Choose a type of favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs) as favored enemies. You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them. When you gain this feature, you also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favored enemies, if they speak one at all. You choose one additional favored enemy, as well as an associated language, at 6th and 14th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of monsters you have encountered on your adventures.

feature:feature:vanish.description: Starting at 14th level, you can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, you can't be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.

feature:feature:feral-senses.description: At 18th level, you gain preternatural senses that help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it. You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't blinded or deafened.

feature:feature:foe-slayer.description: At 20th level, you become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make against one of your favored enemies. You can choose to use this feature before or after the roll, but before any effects of the roll are applied.

feature:feature:rogue:expertise.description: At 1st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with thieves' tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies. At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves' tools) to gain this benefit

feature:feature:sneak-attack.description: Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon. You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't incapacitated, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll. The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table.

feature:feature:thieves-cant.description: During your rogue training you learned thieves' cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation. Only another creature that knows thieves' cant understands such messages. It takes four times longer to convey such a message than it does to speak the same idea plainly. In addition, you understand a set of secret signs and symbols used to convey short, simple messages, such as whether an area is dangerous or the territory of a thieves' guild, whether loot is nearby, or whether the people in an area are easy marks or will provide a safe house for thieves on the run.

feature:feature:cunning-action.description: Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

feature:feature:roguish-archetype.description: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you emulate in the exercise of your rogue abilities, such as Thief. Additional archetypes are available in the original source material. Your archetype choice grants you features at 3rd level and then again at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

feature:feature:uncanny-dodge.description: Starting at 5th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

feature:feature:rogue:evasion.description: Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a red dragon's fiery breath or an ice storm spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

feature:feature:reliable-talent.description: By 11th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

feature:feature:blindsense.description: Starting at 14th level, if you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.

feature:feature:slippery-mind.description: By 15th level, you have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

feature:feature:elusive.description: Beginning at 18th level, you are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated.

feature:feature:stroke-of-luck.description: At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

feature:feature:spellcasting-sorcerer.description: An event in your past, or in the life of a parent or ancestor, left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with arcane magic. This font of magic, whatever its origin, fuels your spells.

feature:feature:sorcerous-origin.description: Choose a sorcerous origin, which describes the source of your innate magical power, such as Draconic Bloodline. Your choice grants you features when you choose it at 1st level and again at 6th, 14th, and 18th level.

feature:feature:font-of-magic.description: At 2nd level, you tap into a deep wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by sorcery points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects. Sorcery Points You have 2 sorcery points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer table. You can never have more sorcery points than shown on the table for your level. You regain all spent sorcery points when you finish a long rest.

feature:feature:flexible-casting-creatin.description: You can transform unexpended sorcery points into one spell slot as a bonus action on your turn. The Creating Spell Slots table shows the cost of creating a spell slot of a given level. You can create spell slots no higher in level than 5th.  Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a long rest.

feature:feature:flexible-casting-convert.description: As a bonus action on your turn, you can expend one spell slot and gain a number of sorcery points equal to the slot's level..

feature:feature:sorcerous-restoration.description: At 20th level, you regain 4 expended sorcery points whenever you finish a short rest.

feature:feature:otherworldly-patron.description: At 1st level, you have struck a bargain with an otherworldly being of your choice, such as the Fiend. Your choice grants you features at 1st level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

feature:feature:pact-magic.description: Your arcane research and the magic bestowed on you by your patron have given you facility with spells.

feature:feature:pact-boon.description: At 3rd level, your otherworldly patron bestows a gift upon you for your loyal service. You gain one of the following features of your choice.

feature:feature:pact-of-the-chain.description: You learn the find familiar spell and can cast it as a ritual. The spell doesn't count against your number of spells known. When you cast the spell, you can choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: imp, pseudodragon, quasit, or sprite. Additionally, when you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its reaction. Your familiar is more cunning than a typical familiar. Its default form can be a reflection of your patron, with imps and quasits tied to the Fiend.

feature:feature:pact-of-the-blade.description: You can use your action to create a pact weapon in your empty hand. You can choose the form that this melee weapon takes each time you create it. You are proficient with it while you wield it. This weapon counts as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. Your pact weapon disappears if it is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more. It also disappears if you use this feature again, if you dismiss the weapon (no action required), or if you die. You can transform one magic weapon into your pact weapon by performing a special ritual while you hold the weapon. You perform the ritual over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a short rest. You can then dismiss the weapon, shunting it into an extradimensional space, and it appears whenever you create your pact weapon thereafter. You can't affect an artifact or a sentient weapon in this way. The weapon ceases being your pact weapon if you die, if you perform the 1-hour ritual on a different weapon, or if you use a 1-hour ritual to break your bond to it. The weapon appears at your feet if it is in the extradimensional space when the bond breaks. If you serve the Fiend, your weapon could be an axe made of black metal and adorned with decorative flames.

feature:feature:pact-of-the-tome.description: Your patron gives you a grimoire called a Book of Shadows. When you gain this feature, choose three cantrips from any class's spell list (the three needn't be from the same list). While the book is on your person, you can cast those cantrips at will. They don't count against your number of cantrips known. If they don't appear on the warlock spell list, they are nonetheless warlock spells for you. If you lose your Book of Shadows, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to receive a replacement from your patron. This ceremony can be performed during a short or long rest, and it destroys the previous book. The book turns to ash when you die. Your Book of Shadows could be a weighty tome bound in demon hide studded with iron, holding spells of conjuration and a wealth of forbidden lore about the sinister regions of the cosmos, a gift of the Fiend.

feature:feature:mystic-arcanum-6th-level.description: At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th- level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum. You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again. At higher levels, you gain more warlock spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th- level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a long rest.

feature:feature:mystic-arcanum-7th-level.description: At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th- level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum. You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again. At higher levels, you gain more warlock spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th- level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a long rest.

feature:feature:mystic-arcanum-8th-level.description: At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th- level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum. You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again. At higher levels, you gain more warlock spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th- level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a long rest.

feature:feature:mystic-arcanum-9th-level.description: At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th- level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum. You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again. At higher levels, you gain more warlock spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th- level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a long rest.

feature:feature:eldritch-master.description: At 20th level, you can draw on your inner reserve of mystical power while entreating your patron to regain expended spell slots. You can spend 1 minute entreating your patron for aid to regain all your expended spell slots from your Pact Magic feature. Once you regain spell slots with this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

feature:feature:spellcasting-wizard.description: As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power.

feature:feature:arcane-recovery.description: You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. For example, if you're a 4th-level wizard, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level spell slot or two 1st-level spell slots.

feature:feature:arcane-tradition.description: When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools, such as Evocation. Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

feature:feature:spell-mastery.description: At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level wizard spell and a 2nd-level wizard spell that are in your spellbook. You can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have them prepared. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal. By spending 8 hours in study, you can exchange one or both of the spells you chose for different spells of the same levels.

feature:feature:signature-spell.description: When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don't count against the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.

feature:feature:hunter-s-bane.description: Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track fey, fiends, and undead and on Intelligence checks to recall lore about them. Your Hemocraft modifier is Intelligence or Wisdom (your choice), and features that call for a save use Hemocraft save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Hemocraft modifier.

feature:feature:blood-maledict.description: You know one blood curse, learning another at 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level, and you can swap one known curse whenever you learn a new one. When you invoke a curse you may amplify it by taking necrotic damage equal to one hemocraft die roll (this damage can't be reduced) to add its Amplify effect. Creatures without blood are immune to unamplified curses. Uses per short or long rest: 1, rising to 2 at 6th level, 3 at 13th, and 4 at 17th. Four further curses are granted only by orders (see each order).

feature:feature:blood-curse-of-the-anxio.description: Bonus action, one creature within 30 feet: until the end of your next turn, Charisma (Intimidation) checks against it have advantage. Amplify: it has disadvantage on its next Wisdom saving throw before the curse ends.

feature:feature:blood-curse-of-binding.description: Bonus action, one Large or smaller creature you can see within 30 feet makes a Strength saving throw; on a failure its speed becomes 0 and it can't take reactions until the end of your next turn. Amplify: works on any size and lasts 1 minute, with a repeat save at the end of each of its turns to end it.

feature:feature:blood-curse-of-bloated-a.description: Bonus action, one creature you can see within 30 feet: until the end of your next turn it has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks and takes 1d8 necrotic damage if it makes more than one attack on its turn. Amplify: lasts 1 minute, and it can end the curse with a Constitution save at the end of each of its turns.

feature:feature:blood-curse-of-exposure.description: Reaction when a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage from an attack or spell: until the end of its next turn it loses resistance to that attack or spell's damage types, including against the triggering damage. Amplify: it instead loses immunity to those types, though it keeps resistance to them until the end of its next turn.

feature:feature:blood-curse-of-the-eyele.description: Reaction when a creature you can see within 30 feet attacks: roll a hemocraft die and subtract it from the attack roll, which you may do after seeing the roll but before the outcome is known. Creatures immune to being blinded are immune. Amplify: every attack roll it makes until the end of its turn takes the penalty, rolled separately each time.

feature:feature:blood-curse-of-the-falle.description: Reaction when a creature you can see within 30 feet drops to 0 hit points: it immediately makes one weapon attack against a target of your choice in its reach or range. Amplify: you can first move it up to half its speed, and it adds your Hemocraft modifier (minimum +1) to the attack roll.

feature:feature:blood-curse-of-the-marke.description: Bonus action, one creature you can see within 30 feet: until the end of your turn, your hits against it with a crimson-rite weapon add one extra hemocraft die of rite damage. Amplify: your next attack roll against it this turn has advantage.

feature:feature:blood-curse-of-the-muddl.description: Bonus action, one creature you can see within 30 feet that is concentrating: it has disadvantage on its next Constitution save to keep concentration before the end of your next turn. Amplify: disadvantage applies to all such concentration saves until the end of your next turn.

feature:feature:crimson-rite.description: As a bonus action, activate a rite you know on one weapon you hold; it lasts until you finish a short or long rest, and activating it costs necrotic damage equal to one hemocraft die roll (can't be reduced). While active, that weapon's attacks are magical and deal an extra hemocraft die of the rite's damage type. A weapon carries one rite at a time and only you gain its benefit. You know one rite, gaining a second at 7th level and a third at 14th.

feature:feature:rite-of-the-dead.description: Rite damage is necrotic. Requires 14th level.

feature:feature:rite-of-the-oracle.description: Rite damage is psychic. Requires 14th level.

feature:feature:rite-of-the-roar.description: Rite damage is thunder. Requires 14th level.

feature:feature:blood-hunter-order.description: Join the Order of the Ghostslayer, Lycan, Mutant, or Profane Soul. The order grants features at 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, and 18th level.

feature:feature:blood-hunter:extra-attac.description: You attack twice when you take the Attack action on your turn.

feature:feature:brand-of-castigation.description: When you deal damage to a creature with a crimson-rite weapon, you can brand it (no action needed). You always know its direction while it shares your plane, and whenever it damages you or a creature you can see within 5 feet of you, it takes psychic damage equal to your Hemocraft modifier (minimum 1). The brand lasts until you dismiss it or brand another creature; dispel magic can end it, treating it as a spell of half your blood hunter level (maximum 9th). Once per short or long rest.

feature:feature:blood-maledict-improveme.description: Blood Maledict usable twice per short or long rest; you learn a second blood curse.

feature:feature:grim-psychometry.description: Advantage on Intelligence (History) checks to recall the dark or tragic past of an object you touch or the place you are in; a high roll may grant brief visions at the DM's discretion.

feature:feature:dark-augmentation.description: Your speed rises by 5 feet, and you add your Hemocraft modifier (minimum +1) to Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws.

feature:feature:brand-of-tethering.description: Brand of Castigation's psychic damage becomes twice your Hemocraft modifier (minimum 2). A branded creature can't Dash, and any attempt it makes to teleport or leave its plane deals 4d6 psychic damage to it and forces a Wisdom save against your Hemocraft save DC; on a failure the attempt fails.

feature:feature:blood-hunter:blood-maled.description: Blood Maledict usable three times per short or long rest.

feature:feature:hardened-soul.description: Advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

feature:feature:blood-hunter:crimson-rit.description: Learn a third crimson rite; the 14th-level rites (Dead, Oracle, Roar) become available.

feature:feature:blood-hunter:base:blood-.description: Blood Maledict usable four times per short or long rest.

feature:feature:sanguine-mastery.description: Once per turn, when a blood hunter feature has you roll a hemocraft die, you may reroll it and pick either result. Scoring a critical hit with a crimson-rite weapon restores one expended Blood Maledict use.

feature:feature:baleful-interdict.description: Once per turn you can put an invisible magical seal on a creature within 30 feet: either when you hit it with a weapon attack (no action) or as a bonus action on one you can see. A seal lasts 1 minute or until burned, a creature bearing your seals is interdicted, and you can see your seals on it. Your seal count is shown in the Seals column (3 at 1st level, rising to 7 at 18th) and all seals return when you finish a short or long rest; if an interdicted creature dies, you can use a bonus action to shift all its seals to another creature you can see within 30 feet of it, with the remaining duration unchanged. Burning Seals: when an interdicted creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage from any source other than a burned seal, you can burn any number of your seals on it (no action, not while incapacitated) to deal 1d6 fire or necrotic damage (your choice) per seal right after that damage; the per-seal damage becomes 2d6 at 5th level, 3d6 at 11th, and 4d6 at 20th. Interdict save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

feature:feature:forked-tongue.description: You speak, read, and write Infernal, and you can speak (but not read or write) two other languages of your choice. After a long rest you can swap one of those two for another language whose name you know, then must finish another long rest before swapping again. At 9th level you gain a third such language and have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks to discern a creature's intentions or sincerity.

feature:feature:combat-mastery.description: Pick one mastery. Bravado: with no armor, your AC is 10 + Dexterity modifier + Charisma modifier, and a shield still works with it. Brutal: when you hit a creature no more than one size larger than you with a melee weapon held in two hands, you can push it 5 feet horizontally and then spend movement to step into the vacated space. Inexorable: +1 to saving throws per hostile creature within 5 feet of you, up to +5. Lies: choose one melee weapon type and use Charisma instead of Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls; you can change the type after a long rest. Lissome: after hitting with a melee weapon attack, you can spend movement to move 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. Unfettered: placing and burning seals reaches 60 feet instead of 30, Infernal Conduit (6th level) reaches 30 feet instead of touch, and being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't give you disadvantage on ranged attacks.

feature:feature:interdiction.description: You learn one interdict boon, gaining more as shown in the Interdict Boons column (1 at 2nd level, 2 at 7th, 3 at 13th, 4 at 18th); each must be of a level you can learn, and whenever you gain an illrigger level you can swap one known boon for another eligible one. Passive boons are always on; you can activate only one non-passive boon per turn. Burning a seal deals its normal seal damage plus the boon's effect, while expending a seal spends an unplaced seal from your pool. 2nd-level boons: Abating Seal (reaction, expend a seal when a creature you can see damages you or an ally within 30 feet: reduce the damage by 1d10 + half your illrigger level, rounded down); Bedevil (on burning a seal, no action: the target subtracts your proficiency bonus from its next saving throw before the end of its next turn); Soul Eater (on burning a seal, no action: gain temporary hit points equal to your illrigger level); Styx's Apathy (on burning a seal, use your reaction: the target can't take reactions until the end of its next turn); Swift Retribution (passive: once per round until the start of your next turn, an opportunity attack provoked by an interdicted creature doesn't use your reaction, if you aren't incapacitated). 7th-level boons: Acheron's Chain (when you place or move a seal with a bonus action on a Large or smaller creature, no action: it makes a Strength save or you pull it 10 feet toward you or grapple it until the end of your next turn, escape DC equal to your interdict save DC); Conflagrant Channel (bonus action, expend a seal: teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see); Eyes of the Gate (action, expend one or more seals on a creature you can see within 60 feet: on a failed Wisdom save, which it can choose to fail, you are linked to it for 1 hour per seal or until you use the boon again; while it is within 300 feet you can use an action to perceive through its senses, including special senses, until you use an action to stop, being blind and deaf to your own meanwhile, and you can place, burn, and use boons as if in its space, which alerts it and lets it use an action to repeat the save to end the link); Shadow Shroud (bonus action, expend a seal: you or a creature you touch gains +2 AC for 1 minute); Unleash Hell (when you burn one or more seals, use your reaction: each chosen creature within 5 feet of the target makes a Dexterity save, taking the same amount and type of damage the seals dealt on a failure or half on a success); Vengeful Shot (reaction, expend a seal when a creature makes a ranged attack against you or an ally you can see within 30 feet: make a ranged weapon attack against it that deals extra damage equal to half your illrigger level, rounded down, on a hit). 13th-level boons: Dis's Onslaught (passive: each time you place or move a seal with a bonus action, you can make one weapon attack as part of it); Flash of Brimstone (when you place or move a seal, no action: teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of the target); Hellish Frenzy (at the start of your turn within 30 feet of an interdicted creature, expend a seal: until the start of your next turn your speed doubles, you gain +2 AC, and the Attack action grants one extra weapon attack); Hellsight (action, expend a seal: truesight 60 feet for 1 hour); Impaling Shot (after hitting an interdicted creature with a ranged weapon attack, bonus action and expend a seal: it takes a penalty to AC equal to your proficiency bonus until the end of your next turn); Iron Gaol (action, touch a creature and expend four seals: on a failed Charisma save it is pulled into a prison in Hell; a creature native to Hell or of level or CR 4 or lower stays there and must find its own way out, otherwise it returns to its space or the nearest unoccupied one after 1 minute and can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to return early); Last Word (when you drop to 0 hit points with unplaced seals, no action: expend up to 3 seals and roll 3d6 per seal; chosen creatures within 30 feet make a Dexterity save, taking that much fire damage on a failure or half on a success, and if at least one creature is damaged you regain hit points equal to the total rolled); Soul's Doom (when you place or move a seal with a bonus action: for 1 minute that creature takes extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus whenever it takes damage).

feature:feature:diabolic-contract.description: You choose your subclass, an archdevil's contract: Architect of Ruin (Asmodeus), Hellspeaker (Moloch), Painkiller (Dispater), Sanguine Knight (Sutekh), or Shadowmaster (Belial). It grants features at 3rd, 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

feature:feature:invoke-hell.description: Your Diabolic Contract gives you two Invoke Hell options. You pick one each time you use this feature, then must finish a short or long rest before using it again. Any saving throw it calls for uses your interdict save DC.

feature:feature:illrigger:extra-attack.description: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you attack twice instead of once.

feature:feature:infernal-conduit.description: You have a pool of d10 Infernal Conduit dice (3 at 6th level, rising to 10 at 19th, per the class table) that refills on a long rest. As an action, touch another creature and spend one or more dice; it makes a Constitution save against your interdict save DC (it may fail willingly), and you roll the spent dice and pick an effect. Invigorate: on a failure it regains hit points equal to the roll, on a success half that, and either way you take necrotic damage equal to the full roll that can't be reduced; if this drops you to 0 hit points you fall unconscious but are stable. Devour: on a failure it takes necrotic damage equal to the roll and you regain that many hit points, on a success it takes half and you regain hit points equal to the damage dealt; this damage can't be reduced. Starting at 11th level, a creature that fails its save against this feature also gains one level of exhaustion (removable normally), but no creature can have more than three exhaustion levels total from illriggers' Infernal Conduit.

feature:feature:forked-tongue-improvemen.description: You gain a third extra spoken language and advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks to read a creature's intentions or sincerity (see Forked Tongue).

feature:feature:blood-price.description: When you fail a saving throw, you can spend one Hit Die, roll it, and add the result to the save.

feature:feature:infernal-conduit-improve.description: A creature that fails its save against your Infernal Conduit also gains one level of exhaustion, capped at three total levels from all illriggers' Infernal Conduit features.

feature:feature:terrorizing-force.description: Pick cold, fire, necrotic, or poison; your weapon hits deal an extra 1d8 damage of that type. You can change the type after a long rest.

feature:feature:superior-interdict.description: Your seal damage ignores the target's damage resistances. Also, when you have no seals left you can use a bonus action to regain one, once per long rest.

feature:feature:infernal-majesty.description: As a bonus action, once per long rest, you take on a portion of your archdevil's might for 10 minutes: resistance to cold, fire, and necrotic damage; a 60-foot flying speed from wings; Blood Price also deals damage equal to the Hit Die roll to an enemy you can see within 10 feet; and Terrorizing Force deals 2d8 instead of 1d8. If you die during this time you can have your body burn away (leaving your gear), and it reforms somewhere in Hell 1d6 days later, alive with all hit points.

feature:feature:master-of-hell.description: As an action, once per long rest, you call a hellstorm filling a 50-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you can see within 150 feet, choosing one effect against each enemy in it. Inferno: Dexterity save, 5d10 fire plus 5d10 necrotic damage and burning for 1 minute on a failure (half and no burning on a success); a burning creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, taking 1d10 fire plus 1d10 necrotic on a failure or ending the burn on a success, and nonmagical means can't put it out. Pestilence: Constitution save, 5d10 poison plus 5d10 necrotic damage and poisoned for 1 minute on a failure (half and not poisoned on a success). Darkness: Constitution save, 10d10 cold damage on a failure or half on a success, and the gloom lasts 1 minute, blinding enemies in the area for the duration or until they leave it.

feature:feature:investigator:expertise.description: Pick two of your skill proficiencies; you add double your proficiency bonus to ability checks using them. At 6th level, pick two more.

feature:feature:ritualist.description: You keep a grimoire of ritual spells and use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for them (spell save DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier; spell attack modifier proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier). Your saves and attacks for investigator rituals and spells granted by this class's features also use Intelligence. Certain spells marked on the Investigator Spells list count as rituals for you, so you can scribe them and cast them as rituals.

feature:feature:grimoire.description: Your grimoire starts with four 1st-level spells that carry the ritual tag, chosen from any class's lists; you can cast its spells only as rituals unless you know them some other way. Each investigator level adds one free ritual from the Investigator Spells list, capped at the level in the Ritual Level column. Rituals from that list found while adventuring can be copied in if their level is within your cap, costing 2 hours and 50 gp of ink per spell level.

feature:feature:myths-and-legends.description: Intelligence checks made to research creatures, spells, or other ancient or secret lore are made with advantage.

feature:feature:rushed-incantation.description: As a bonus action, you can complete any grimoire ritual whose casting time is 1 action or 1 bonus action, ignoring material components worth 100 gp or less. Uses equal your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1), restored on a long rest; you gain one extra use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level (up to Intelligence modifier + 4).

feature:feature:occult-specialization.description: Choose a specialization, which grants features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 14th level. Specializations also grant trinkets: using any trinket spends one use, and you get 1 use per short or long rest, rising to 2 at 5th level, 3 at 11th, and 4 at 17th.

feature:feature:exploit-weakness.description: Once per turn when a weapon attack hits, the target counts as vulnerable to that weapon's damage, but only the weapon's damage dice and your ability modifier are doubled (not extra damage from spells, items, feats, or features like Sneak Attack). That attack and every other attack against the target until the start of your next turn count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

feature:feature:investigator:base:expert.description: Choose two more skill proficiencies to gain the Expertise benefit.

feature:feature:opportunistic-piety.description: Pick one of these effects each time; afterward you need a short or long rest before using the feature again. Banish: cast banishment without a spell slot, and a Fey, Fiend, or Undead that fails the save also takes radiant damage equal to your level. Miracle Healing: as an action, a willing creature you touch regains hit points equal to twice your investigator level (no effect on Undead or Constructs). Warding: as an action, mark a creature within 5 feet; for 1 minute, any Aberration, Celestial, Fey, Fiend, or Undead that touches it or hits it with a melee attack takes 1d12 radiant damage.

feature:feature:supernatural-resolve.description: You can't be charmed or possessed, and you resist necrotic and psychic damage.

feature:feature:finisher.description: Once per turn when you take the Attack action and hit with a weapon attack, add 2d8 damage, or 4d8 instead if the target is below half its hit points.

feature:feature:enigma-arcane.description: Once per long rest, cast one of mirage arcane, plane shift, reverse gravity, sequester, or teleport without a spell slot.

feature:feature:enigma-arcane-improvemen.description: Add a second slot-free casting, once per long rest, chosen from antimagic field, glibness, maze, or mind blank.

feature:feature:investigator:enigma-arca.description: Add a third slot-free casting, once per long rest, chosen from astral projection, gate, or weird.

feature:feature:exorcist.description: You can cast protection from evil and good with no spell slot and no material components.

feature:feature:spellbinder.description: Designate five grimoire rituals with a casting time of 1 action. You can cast them as a bonus action without spending Rushed Incantation uses and without holding your grimoire, ignoring material components worth 100 gp or less.

feature:feature:sentinel-s-stand.description: Choose one option. Armor Proficiency: you gain heavy armor proficiency. Primal Toughness: your hit point maximum rises by 1 + your Constitution modifier, and by 1 more each time you gain a warden level. Stalwart Spirit: you gain proficiency in one saving throw of your choice.

feature:feature:warden-s-grasp.description: As a bonus action, you root yourself: until the start of your next turn you can't move, and each Large or smaller creature you choose within 5 feet can't willingly move away from you unless it takes the Disengage action first. The range becomes 10 feet at 14th level.

feature:feature:warden-s-mark.description: As a bonus action, mark a creature you can see within 30 feet. While it is within 5 feet of you, it has disadvantage on attack rolls that don't target you. The mark lasts 1 minute, ending early if you mark another creature, are incapacitated, or die. From 11th level, when you take the Attack action you can make one extra attack as part of it against a creature you have marked.

feature:feature:champion-s-call.description: Choose a call, which grants features at 3rd, 6th, 13th, and 20th level.

feature:feature:warden-s-resolve.description: While below half your hit point maximum, you resist bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. From 17th level, this becomes resistance to all damage other than psychic.

feature:feature:font-of-life.description: As an action, end one disease or one condition on yourself (blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, paralyzed, or poisoned), even if that condition would normally stop you from acting. Once per short or long rest. From 15th level, using it can also raise your hit points to half your maximum if they were lower, once per long rest.

feature:feature:sentinel-s-step.description: Choose one option. Earthstrength: your carrying capacity doubles, and you have advantage on checks and saves against being pushed against your will or knocked prone. Thundering Charge: in the first round of combat, your speed rises by 30 feet and your first melee weapon attack has advantage. Wildblood: you can't be surprised while conscious, and your passive Wisdom (Perception) and passive Intelligence (Investigation) scores gain +5.

feature:feature:undying.description: Once per long rest, when you drop to 0 hit points without being killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead.

feature:feature:interrupt.description: When a creature hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to cost it one of its remaining attacks this turn, if it has any.

feature:feature:mark-improvement.description: Taking the Attack action lets you make one extra attack as part of it against a creature you have marked.

feature:feature:grasp-improvement.description: Warden's Grasp now reaches creatures within 10 feet.

feature:feature:font-of-life-improvement.description: Font of Life can also restore your hit points to half your maximum if they were lower, once per long rest.

feature:feature:warden-s-resolve-improve.description: While below half your hit point maximum, you resist all damage except psychic.

feature:feature:sentinel-s-soul.description: Choose one option. Ageless Guardian: immunity to poison and disease, no need for food or water, no frailty of age and no magical aging (you can still die of old age), plus advantage on Constitution saves. Eyes of the Mountain: tremorsense 15 feet, awareness of hidden or invisible creatures within 30 feet, plus advantage on Dexterity saves. Impenetrable Mind: your thoughts can't be read and you can't be charmed or frightened, plus advantage on Wisdom saves.

feature:feature:spellcasting-warmage.description: Intelligence is your casting ability; you cast only cantrips through this class. You start with four cantrips from the class spell list and gain more per the Cantrips Known column, and each time you gain a warmage level you may swap one known warmage cantrip for another. Spell save DC is 8 + proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier; spell attack modifier is proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. An arcane focus works as your spellcasting focus.

feature:feature:arcane-initiation.description: Pick the origin of your magic at 1st level; each grants two cantrips that are extra and don't count toward your warmage cantrips known. Options: Adventurer (mage hand and ray of frost); Circus Performer (dancing lights and minor illusion); Eldritch Event (chill touch and message); Mercenary (arc blade and true strike); Self-Taught (fire bolt and light); Survival (druidcraft and shillelagh); Temple (sacred flame and spare the dying); Tower Apprentice (prestidigitation and shocking grasp).

feature:feature:arcane-initiation-advent.description: You gain the mage hand and ray of frost cantrips; they don't count against your warmage cantrips known.

feature:feature:arcane-initiation-circus.description: You gain the dancing lights and minor illusion cantrips; they don't count against your warmage cantrips known.

feature:feature:arcane-initiation-eldrit.description: You gain the chill touch and message cantrips; they don't count against your warmage cantrips known.

feature:feature:arcane-initiation-mercen.description: You gain the arc blade and true strike cantrips; they don't count against your warmage cantrips known.

feature:feature:arcane-initiation-self-t.description: You gain the fire bolt and light cantrips; they don't count against your warmage cantrips known.

feature:feature:arcane-initiation-surviv.description: You gain the druidcraft and shillelagh cantrips; they don't count against your warmage cantrips known.

feature:feature:arcane-initiation-temple.description: You gain the sacred flame and spare the dying cantrips; they don't count against your warmage cantrips known.

feature:feature:arcane-initiation-tower-.description: You gain the prestidigitation and shocking grasp cantrips; they don't count against your warmage cantrips known.

feature:feature:arcane-fighting-style.description: At 1st level choose one magical fighting style: Blaster (Add 1 to the spell save DC of your warmage cantrips); Deflector (With at least one free hand, when a spell attack or ranged weapon attack hits you, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC against that attack, possibly turning it into a miss); Resistive (You get +1 AC while wearing light armor or while mage armor is on you); Sniper (Your ranged spell attack rolls gain +1, and your warmage cantrips ignore half cover); Striker (When a cantrip that uses a melee attack hits and either beats the target's AC by 5 or more or is a critical hit, you can add your proficiency bonus to the damage).

feature:feature:arcane-fighting-style-bl.description: Add 1 to the spell save DC of your warmage cantrips.

feature:feature:arcane-fighting-style-de.description: With at least one free hand, when a spell attack or ranged weapon attack hits you, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC against that attack, possibly turning it into a miss.

feature:feature:arcane-fighting-style-re.description: You get +1 AC while wearing light armor or while mage armor is on you.

feature:feature:arcane-fighting-style-sn.description: Your ranged spell attack rolls gain +1, and your warmage cantrips ignore half cover.

feature:feature:arcane-fighting-style-st.description: When a cantrip that uses a melee attack hits and either beats the target's AC by 5 or more or is a critical hit, you can add your proficiency bonus to the damage.

feature:feature:warmage-edge.description: Once on each of your turns when a warmage cantrip deals damage, add your Intelligence modifier to one of its damage rolls. From 5th level you also add the extra dice listed in the Cantrip Bonus Dice column (1 at 5th, 2 at 11th, 3 at 17th) to your warmage cantrip damage; for example, a 5th-level warmage's fire bolt deals 3d10 + Intelligence modifier fire damage.

feature:feature:warmage-tricks.description: You know two warmage tricks at 2nd level and learn more per the Tricks Known column (up to 10). Whenever you gain a warmage level you may replace one known trick with another whose prerequisites you meet. Level prerequisites refer to warmage level, and you can take a trick at the same level you meet its prerequisites.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-bishop-s-m.description: Prerequisite: 10th level, House of Bishops. Disengage is a bonus action for you, and when you take it that way your walking speed rises by 10 feet until your turn ends.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-blasting-c.description: Once per turn, when a warmage cantrip deals force damage to a creature, you can shove it up to 10 feet straight away from you.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-blinding-l.description: Prerequisite: light cantrip. When you cast light on an object you hold, you can flash it at a creature you can see within 10 feet; it makes a Constitution save against your spell save DC or is blinded until the start of your next turn. A creature that fails gains advantage on saves against this trick for 24 hours.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-castle.description: Prerequisite: 10th level, House of Rooks. As an action, you and a willing Small or Medium creature you can see within 120 feet teleport to trade places. Once per short or long rest.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-chivalrous.description: Prerequisite: House of Knights. Gain proficiency in Insight and Persuasion and advantage on ability checks to interact with nobility; other creatures can always tell when you are speaking truthfully.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-cloak-of-f.description: Prerequisite: House of Rooks. With no armor and no shield, your AC is 10 + Dexterity modifier + Intelligence modifier.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-commander-.description: Prerequisite: House of Kings. You can cast find steed at will without a spell slot, and the steed's hit point maximum increases by your warmage level.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-corrosive-.description: Once per turn, when a warmage cantrip deals acid damage to a creature, the next attack roll made against it before the start of your next turn treats its AC as reduced by 1d4 for that attack.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-directed-m.description: Prerequisite: 10th level, House of Lancers. Once per turn, when you crit with a melee attack or drop a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make an unarmed strike against another target (lunging to it if it is within Shock Trooper range); a hit deals an extra 1d8 force damage.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-draining-c.description: When a warmage cantrip deals necrotic or poison damage to a hostile creature, you gain temporary hit points equal to half your warmage level for 1 minute.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-encryptogr.description: Prerequisite: cryptogram cantrip. Your cryptogram messages can hold 20 characters instead of 8, and only the intended recipient can read them.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-explosive-.description: Once per turn, when a warmage cantrip deals fire damage to a creature, every other creature within 5 feet of it (not you) makes a Dexterity save against your spell save DC or takes half the fire damage the target took.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-extended-r.description: Warmage cantrips with a range of 5 feet or more have their range doubled.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-field-medi.description: Prerequisite: House of Bishops. You learn spare the dying as a bonus cantrip. When you cast it on a creature at 0 hit points, it regains 1 hit point and gains temporary hit points equal to your warmage level for 1 minute; a creature can benefit from this healing once per long rest.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-flexible-r.description: Hostile creatures within 5 feet don't give you disadvantage on ranged spell attacks, and warmage cantrips that use a melee spell attack reach 10 feet.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-fold.description: Prerequisite: 10th level, House of Cards. When an attack hits you, you can use your reaction and discard your whole Deck of Fate hand to cast shield without a slot. Once per short or long rest.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-gamble.description: Prerequisite: cheat cantrip, House of Cards or House of Dice. The cheat cantrip is always in effect on you, and once per short or long rest you can reroll an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-icy-cantri.description: Once per turn, when a warmage cantrip deals cold damage to a creature, its first attack roll before the end of its next turn takes a 1d4 penalty.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-infinite-v.description: Prerequisite: prestidigitation cantrip. Prestidigitation can mimic any non-damaging cantrip, even one off the warmage list, if you pass a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check (otherwise the casting fails). The mimicked cantrip uses Intelligence and counts as a warmage cantrip.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-knight-s-a.description: Prerequisite: 10th level, House of Knights, force buckler cantrip. Force buckler can be held with concentration for up to 1 minute and is not ended early by being hit.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-leading-ed.description: Prerequisite: House of Lancers. Attacks made against you during the first round of combat have disadvantage.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-lieutenant.description: Prerequisite: 10th level, House of Kings. You can cast command at will without a spell slot.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-mage-hand-.description: Prerequisite: mage hand cantrip. When you cast mage hand, and as a bonus action on later turns, the hand can: Press (pushes on a Large or smaller creature within 5 feet; each foot it moves in a direction you pick costs it 1 extra foot, lasting until the spell ends or you switch effects), Punch (melee spell attack against a creature or object within 5 feet for 1d6 force damage), or Seize (a Tiny creature must beat your spell save DC with Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) or be grappled until it uses an action to escape, the spell ends, or you switch effects).

feature:feature:warmage-trick-minor-shad.description: Prerequisite: minor illusion cantrip. An object image from minor illusion can be made semi-real (max 5-foot cube, AC 10, 5 hit points, 5 pounds; one at a time, requires concentration). If it depicts something harmful, a creature entering its cube or starting its turn there makes an Intelligence save or takes 1d6 damage of a fitting type, rising to 2d6 at 5th, 3d6 at 11th, and 4d6 at 17th level. This damage can't trigger Warmage Edge or tricks.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-mystical-a.description: You can cast mage armor on yourself at will without a spell slot or components.

Prerequisite: quickstep or springheel cantrip. Quickstep grants +20 feet of speed instead of +10, springheel grants +20 feet of jump distance instead of +10, and if you know both you can cast them with the same bonus action.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-mystical-v.description: You can cast detect magic at will without a spell slot.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-mystical-w.description: Prerequisite: force weapon or magic daggers cantrip. Once per turn, when you roll a 1 on the d20 for an attack with force weapon or magic daggers, reroll it and use the new result.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-phantom-ho.description: Prerequisite: phantom grapnel cantrip. Phantom grapnel can be cast as a bonus action with its range cut to 15 feet; cast as an action, it pulls creatures an additional 10 feet toward you.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-rapid-fort.description: Prerequisite: mending cantrip. Mending can be cast as a bonus action. Cast as an action, it can instead fully restore a nonmagical object up to 10 cubic feet (1 cubic foot if intricate) with at least half its parts present, or build simple fortifications up to 10 cubic feet (sealing a door, boarding a window, a short stone wall) if the materials are on hand.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-severe-can.description: A creature that rolls a 1 on a save against your warmage cantrip fails automatically and takes double the damage dice, as with a critical hit (only that creature).

feature:feature:warmage-trick-signature-.description: Prerequisite: 5th level. After a long rest, mark a simple weapon as your magical signature focus (until you use the trick again). It works as a warmage spellcasting focus, you can summon it to hand as a bonus action while on the same plane, and you can use Intelligence for attack rolls with it. It holds charges equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1); spend one when it or a cantrip cast through it damages a creature to add 1d8 force damage. Charges return on a long rest.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-silent-can.description: Once per turn, when a warmage cantrip deals thunder damage to a hostile creature, you can create a 15-foot-diameter sphere of silence (as the silence spell) centered on you or the target, lasting until the start of your next turn.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-snake-eyes.description: Prerequisite: 10th level, House of Dice. When a Die of Fate you roll shows 1 or 2, you keep it instead of passing it to the GM.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-split-fire.description: Prerequisite: 5th level. A warmage cantrip that makes a single spell attack can instead target several different creatures, up to the number of its damage dice, with a separate attack roll each; divide the damage dice among them, at least one die per target (fire bolt's 3d10 could be 1d10 x 3, 1d10 + 2d10, or 3d10 on one target).

feature:feature:warmage-trick-static-can.description: When a warmage cantrip deals lightning damage to a hostile creature, you hold a charge until the start of your next turn; while charged, when a creature you can see within 5 feet damages you, you can use your reaction to deal lightning damage to it equal to half your warmage level.

feature:feature:warmage-trick-unerring-s.description: Prerequisite: 10th level, true strike cantrip. You can maintain true strike for a number of rounds equal to your Intelligence modifier, and while you concentrate you have advantage on your first attack roll against the target on each of your turns.

feature:feature:warmage-house.description: Choose a Warmage House at 3rd level: House of Bishops, House of Cards, House of Dice, House of Kings, House of Knights, House of Lancers, House of Pawns, House of Rooks. It grants features at 3rd, 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level.

feature:feature:arcane-surge.description: On your turn, when a warmage cantrip deals damage, you can double the number of damage dice the spell deals. It can't be used on a critical hit. Once per short or long rest, twice per rest from 11th level.

feature:feature:tactical-insight.description: Add your Intelligence modifier to saving throws against spells and other magical effects that deal damage.

feature:feature:arcane-surge-improvement.description: You can use Arcane Surge twice between short or long rests.

feature:feature:strategic-deflection.description: When a spell that targets you or includes you in its area forces a save to avoid damage and you succeed, you can use your reaction to redirect it: pick another creature you can see within the spell's range or 30 feet of you (whichever is shorter), possibly the caster, which saves against your spell save DC and on a failure suffers the spell as if you had cast it on it. Once per short or long rest.

feature:feature:master-warmage.description: A cantrip of yours that would deal 4 damage dice deals 5 instead (not counting cantrip bonus dice), and a cantrip that would make 4 attacks makes 5.

feature:feature:spellcasting-witch.description: Charisma-based full spellcasting from the class spell list. You know four cantrips and two 1st-level spells at 1st level, gaining more per the Cantrips Known and Spells Known columns; new spells must be of a level you have slots for, and each witch level you may swap one known spell for another. Slots follow the Witch table and return on a long rest. Spell save DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier; spell attack proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier. You can ritual-cast known witch spells with the ritual tag and use an arcane focus.

feature:feature:witch-s-curse.description: Pick the form of your curse at 1st level: Burned (Resistance to fire damage, and you know produce flame as a bonus cantrip); Drowned (You breathe both air and water and have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed); Feral (Proficiency in Survival; with no armor and no shield, your AC is 12 + Dexterity modifier); Hideous (Proficiency in Intimidation. When you roll initiative, one Humanoid you can see makes a Wisdom save against your spell save DC or is frightened of you until the end of your next turn); Hollow (When you or your familiar drops a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points of your witch level + Charisma modifier (minimum 1)); Infested (Immune to disease. Your familiar can take the form of a swarm of rats from 2nd level and a swarm of insects from 7th level); Loveless (Immune to being charmed); Possessed (Gain one extra witch spell (of a level you have slots for) at 1st, 4th, 8th, and 12th level; these don't count against spells known); Starving (You need no food or drink (potions still work on you) and are immune to the poisoned condition); Visions (You can add your Charisma modifier to initiative rolls); Whispers (You can speak telepathically with any creature you can see within 30 feet that understands at least one language, shared or not).

feature:feature:witch-s-curse-burned.description: Resistance to fire damage, and you know produce flame as a bonus cantrip.

feature:feature:witch-s-curse-drowned.description: You breathe both air and water and have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

feature:feature:witch-s-curse-feral.description: Proficiency in Survival; with no armor and no shield, your AC is 12 + Dexterity modifier.
